newsitem.title: UK: Brussels to clear BT, MCI merger Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brussels to clear BT, MCI merger Wednesday.

text.p: Brussels regulators will on Wednesday clear the largest transatlantic merger in history -- the $20 billion deal between British Telecommunications Plc and America's second biggest long-distance carrier, MCI Communications Corp.

European Competition Commissioner Karl Van Miert told BBC radio in an interview to be broadcast on Tuesday night that Brussels was poised to clear the deal after what he called "very positive co-operation" between the companies and regulators.
"Tomorrow the Commission will certainly take a positive decision on the BT/MCI (deal)," Van Miert told BBC Radio 5 Live's Financial World Tonight in an interview from Strasbourg.
With clearance assured from Brussels and after both BT and MCI shareholders overwhelmingly approved the deal last month, the merger's last remaining hurdle is U.S. regulators.
BT, which declined to comment before being officially notified of the Commission's decision, is confident of winning definitive approval by autumn.
The merger will create a new company called Concert Plc, a "global supercarrier" with annual revenues of more than 25 billion pounds ($40 billion) and 43 million customers.
The deal creates the world's fourth largest telecoms group in terms of sales after Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), America's AT & T Corp and Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG.
The deadline for the EU's verdict on the deal had been June 11, but clearance in the first half of May was expected.

Commission sources have said that clearance hinged on giving telecoms rivals reasonable access to the two partners' transatlantic cable capacity and modifications to BT and MCI's dominant position in the British market for audio and video conferencing.
Van Miert said that BT had offered solutions to two problems identified by competition regulators and that he was "absolutely" unconcerned about Concert wielding too much market muscle.

"BT has been very positive, forthcoming, open-minded about it and put its cards on the table. We identified two problems and they were offering almost immediately the right answers to the problems -- so we said okay, we can go ahead," Van Miert told the BBC.
BT argues that because of the breakneck speed of new technology and the globalisation of the booming $650 billion telecoms market, the merger will bring benefits that BT could not deliver alone.

A deal with MCI opens up the world's largest telecoms market to BT. The United States is home to 40 percent of the largest multinational company headquarters -- the most sought-after clients by global telecoms groups.
BT also hopes to take a share of the lucrative local market through MCI as this is opened up to competition.
BT and MCI currently hold about six percent of the global telecoms market which is expected to top one trillion dollars by 2000 -- but they plan to chase the other 94 percent.

The partnership has already forged alliances around the world, including its latest deal with flagship Spanish operator Telefonica De Espana, which allows Concert to tap the booming Latin America telecoms market through Telefonica's international unit TISA.

Concert wants to provide clients around the globe with local, long distance, international and mobile phone services as well as multi-media, Internet-based services and systems integration for business clients.

The group plans to be represented in key countries across the world so it can focus on winning high-margin, multinational clients that analysts estimate account for about 15-20 percent of global telecoms revenue.
Concert's last gap in the geographical patchwork it has spun remains Asia. BT has been courting Japan's titan NTT for years -- so far unsuccessfully.
($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
